gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many days each watch lasts per charge with one hour of GPS HYROX training a day. Each rival repeats the maker's 'up to N days' and 'N h GPS' separately, and none combines them into one figure.
standout_why: I opened our page (dealectric.com/best-watch-for-hyrox-under-150). It lists the rated days and GPS hours side by side but works out no per-session or per-day figure. I also opened Amazfit's US store data for the Bip 6, Active 2 and Bip Max, plus COROS's PACE 3 page; none of them works it out either. The roxgrit.com fetch failed on a certificate error, and Wareable, Android Authority, Know Your Mobile and WearableBeat all returned 403, so I couldn't check them. Search snippets suggest Wareable and WearableBeat print measured drain (6% per 30-minute GPS session on the Bip 6; about 10% per GPS hour on the Active 2), so the rivals may already have part of this. I could only compute the figure for the two watches over budget (COROS PACE 3, Garmin FR55), because Amazfit's spec pages kept returning HTTP 429 and I never got their GPS-hour figures from a page I opened. That's why this scores 1.
decides: This confirms the pick and doesn't change it. Among the sourced watches, the over-budget COROS PACE 3 lasts about 10.7 days at one GPS hour a day and the Garmin FR55 about 8.2. If Amazfit's own pages confirm the 14 d / 32 h and 10 d / 21 h figures, the Bip 6 comes out around 9.7 days and the Active 2 around 6.8. That would make the $79.99 Bip 6 the longest-lasting watch under $150 with a HYROX mode, and it would put the $99.99 Active 2 behind the FR55 on battery. The Active 2 would then keep only its Singles, Doubles and Relay race formats and its display as reasons to choose it.
